rewrites.0C24F464: The runway limits the peak hours until its relief arrives, and outside the Metro the product exists but is hard to reach without a car and uneven to stay in.
rewrites.0349616B: Eleven of 27 international routes run above an 80% load factor and carriers are expected to price before adding seats, so the province must win frequency and larger aircraft before runway relief in about 2033.
rewrites.01E1DCFB: On air access the evidence describes a timing problem. The fares forecast covers the mature long-haul routes only, and no fare data yet tests it. The five regional markets that also run above an 80% load factor are named for more capacity. The hub routes still have room, with Dubai at 72.3%, Addis Ababa at 71.9% and Doha at 65.2%. On those routes marketing can still fill seats.[^300]
rewrites.50E733F8: Relief also comes in the wrong order: the certain fix comes last, and the earliest large option is the least certain. George doubles its capacity but flies domestic routes only, and Cape Winelands stays a scenario until finance, licensing and carriers are shown. The province's aviation strategy identifies a possible upgrade that would let George handle international traffic. No airline is among the 16 organisations whose views this report draws on, so carriers' views on frequency and aircraft size are untested.[^301]
rewrites.2A5B0E41: The approach splits the air agenda by horizon. Until runway relief arrives in about 2033, the first job is to fill and enlarge what already flies. The near-term moves are added frequency from Emirates, Qatar Airways and Ethiopian Airlines, with airline incentives coordinated through Cape Town Air Access. Route cases for India and China are the long-term move. Wesgro also presses for more seats to Luanda, Maputo, Gaborone, Harare and Mauritius, the five regional markets above an 80% load factor.[^302]
rewrites.35B4394D: The vehicle already exists. Cape Town Air Access has worked since 2015 as a partnership of six public bodies and private-sector partners, which fund and advise it. The six are the Western Cape Government, the City of Cape Town, Cape Town Tourism, Wesgro, SA Tourism and ACSA, and the private partners named in 2026 are the V&A Waterfront and DHL. The action is to scale and re-term that partnership, not to design a fund. Five things are new. Support is sized to the seats the target requires (section 2.4). Winter seat retention becomes an explicit purpose. Budgets are ring-fenced by corridor. The partners make multi-year commitments. Hub-closure scenarios shape where support goes.[^304]
rewrites.51678D74: The programme works on the airline's decision, not the visitor's. A carrier on a mature long-haul route seeks revenue through fares, yet there is tactical room for added frequency and larger aircraft. Joint marketing and ring-fenced route support lower the carrier's risk on extra capacity. The province then buys seats, not higher fares. Belly cargo strengthens the case. Cape Town International is the province's only airport for international air freight, all of it carried in passenger aircraft. Exports made up 67% of its air freight in 2023. New Zealand tied marketing budgets to long-haul corridors and designed campaigns around airline breakeven. Its reported 2023/24 result is more than 16,000 incremental bookings and a return of about NZ$55 million (section 2.2).[^305]
rewrites.21B4F264: Cruise has room to grow at the berth Cape Town already has. The equipped berth can take 150 or more calls a season; it handled 83 in 2024/25, and the province received 64 cruise liner visits in 2025/26. The 2025/26 season brought R1.47 billion of spending and added R1.35 billion to provincial GDP-R, against about R1.79 billion after displacement a season earlier. The berth is not what limits growth.[^307]
rewrites.35C3B454: International passengers drive the value (section 2.4). In 2024/25, the last season with a full study in hand, world cruises made up 42 of the 79 vessel visits. Their passengers added R802 million to provincial GDP-R, 73% of what all passengers added. That season also earned R1.326 billion of net foreign exchange and R259 million in taxes. In 2025/26 cruise generated about R1 billion of foreign exchange.[^308]
rewrites.12578553: The approach works on the circuit and the shore, with the berth Cape Town already has. Cruise Cape Town leads. In 2027 it designs a circuit compact with partner ports and lines and a call-day flow plan with the flagship operators. In the same year it designs the Mossel Bay excursion packages and one definition of a call for reporting against the 250. Shore programmes beyond the flagship sites follow in 2028, with marketing to homeport, expedition and shoulder-season operators and community product on cruise-operator channels (section 4.3). Saldanha Bay waits until demand is proven, because its port capital serves iron ore.
rewrites.254C660F: Wesgro does not build transport. It makes existing transport usable for visitors and gathers the demand that makes shuttles pay. The Department of Mobility holds the transport lever, and Wesgro's Tourism unit convenes the work. Wesgro pilots shuttle aggregation and transfers sold inside itineraries in 2027 and 2028, and shuttle products run from 2029. The April 2025 draft land transport framework targets MyCiTi Phase 2A to Khayelitsha and Mitchells Plain for 2027, which would bring township product within reach sooner. The Department of Mobility's draft Tourism Transport Strategy adds the airport leg and touring-route signage, so Wesgro also sells airport transfers inside itineraries.[^320]
rewrites.15F41394: The evidence locates the constraint. It is less about creating new attractions and more about turning existing assets into complete, accessible visitor experiences. Each route falls short on something different: accommodation and bookability on the West Coast, bookability on Route 62 and depth beyond Hermanus on the Whale Coast. The Cape Winelands and the Garden Route fall short only on safety (section 2.4).[^326]
rewrites.79F11912: Non-wine diversification in the Cape Winelands is strategy, not committed capital; De Hoop lacks accommodation investment; Overberg year-round product is unfunded
rewrites.6D225156: Wesgro works outward from strength. The Garden Route, the Cape Winelands and the Overberg already have strong underlying product and need connectivity, packaging and service depth. Wesgro packages Route 62 and the West Coast as slow-travel products. In 2027 and 2028 the Tourism unit designs bookable itineraries for all six touring routes. Delivery starts from 2029 on the Garden Route, the Cape Winelands and the Overberg, which are closest to ready. It moves to Route 62 and the West Coast once their product is online (objective 3; section 4.3).[^328]
rewrites.6A9FCD51: The first product is the regional add-on. A two-to-three-night extension to a Cape Town stay, with the transfer included, is the simplest regional product to sell and the one the extension strategy in objective 5 needs. The Cape Winelands, the Whale Coast and the Garden Route can each supply one from existing product, and Wesgro designs the add-ons in 2027.
rewrites.7494407F: Build a two-to-three-night regional add-on for each of the Cape Winelands, the Whale Coast and the Garden Route, with transfers included, for sale as an extension to a Cape Town stay (objective 5)
rewrites.26A6F736: Chile ran Santiago, Valparaíso, the wine valleys and Patagonia as one portfolio. It reports longer stays and shoulder-season revenue from the approach, though it gives no figure for either. The change for the Western Cape is to sell experiences as curated journeys and move from asset marketing to experience-led packaging. The condition is that the other entries keep pace. Itineraries sell only if the product can be booked (objective 3), reached without a car (objective 9) and stayed in. Without beds, a packaged route stays a day trip from Cape Town.[^331]
rewrites.12AF7CC1: The experience is weakest at the arrival gate and at the periphery. Online mentions of Cape Town are most negative about the international airport (section 2.1). Further out, readiness falls with distance from the Metro (section 2.4). Accommodation readiness drops from 4.7 in the Metro to 2.0 in the Central Karoo.[^333]
rewrites.2F4AE489: Two measures are missing. No source counts rooms or beds by district and type, short-term rentals included, and none gives a visitor satisfaction score.
rewrites.557FD955: Two strands join the charter. Wesgro builds accessible journeys as saleable itineraries and tests them end to end with lived-experience partners. It publishes their verified access information. Guide registration is run as a service, with its performance published.
rewrites.269C7A97: Quality governance was Valencia's primary lever. Its Qualitur programme and SICTED quality system raised service consistency, reputation and repeat visitation. International visitors to the city reached 3.5 million in 2024, 24.4% above 2019 (section 2.2). Singapore's tourism board used a hotel industry transformation map, a hotel rejuvenation fund and the Hotels Act. The aim was to move from short stopovers towards longer stays and higher spend. The condition is that small businesses can comply. The compliance burden and skills shortages are the main risks, so the charter needs SMME support from the start and the skills work in objective 20.[^337]
rewrites.6A6002A7: The evidence holds counts but not limits. In 2023 Boulders drew 762,494 visitors, up 60.2% on 2022. Cape Point, counted as the Cape of Good Hope, drew 940,399, up 49.0%. Section 2.4 gives the other flagships' counts. With 55.4% of international tourists going there, Cape Point is a flagship in its own right. No source yet gives permitted capacity for these sites. Without limits, the province cannot set caps, price the peak or show that steering visitors works.[^341]
rewrites.2456F2C0: Timed entry has a mixed record, which is why each pilot carries a stop rule. Rocky Mountain made day-use access permanent after pilots, while Arches and Yosemite dropped reservations in 2026 (Appendix A3). The pilots watch queues, conservation outcomes, excluded visits and neighbouring businesses together.
